name: Kang-Petrov Arms KPM-12 'Steadfast'
description:
The KPM-12 Steadfast is a battle-DMR hybrid that sacrifices extreme accuracy for sustained-fire capability. Where conventional DMRs are precision instruments that demand careful shooting, the Steadfast is designed for designated marksmen who operate as part of assault elements and need to maintain precision fire while moving and shooting rapidly. The weapon chambers 7.62mm caseless with a heavy barrel that resists thermal shift during sustained engagement.

The Steadfast's BCI integration focuses on moving-target engagement rather than static precision. The AI tracks target movement vectors and provides a continuously updated lead indicator in the neural overlay, allowing the marksman to maintain effective fire on moving targets at ranges up to 500 meters. The weapon's 1.5-MOA accuracy is modest by DMR standards but maintained consistently through high round counts and rapid-fire sequences.

Kang-Petrov prices the Steadfast at Φ3,500, positioning it between their Equalizer and premium competitors. Its customers are operators who need a marksman's reach with a rifleman's tempo — squad-level marksmen who engage targets of opportunity while keeping pace with their assault element rather than providing static overwatch. The weapon fills a role that traditional DMR doctrine doesn't acknowledge: the moving marksman.
specifications:
caliber: 7.62mm caseless
effective_range: 500m (moving engagement), 650m (static)
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic (rapid capable)
magazine_capacity: 20 rounds
weight: 4.5 kg
tactical_use: The Steadfast enables precision fire from assault elements in motion. Traditional DMR doctrine positions the marksman in a static overwatch role, but many operations require the marksman to advance with the squad. The KPM-12's moving-target AI and thermal-resistant barrel maintain engagement capability during the kind of rapid, mobile shooting that would degrade a traditional precision rifle's accuracy. The weapon trades peak accuracy for consistency under stress.
cultural_context: The Steadfast represents a doctrinal shift in how designated marksmen are employed. Rather than separating the marksman from the squad, the KPM-12 integrates them into the assault element as a mobile precision asset. This approach appeals to freelance teams where separating a member for static overwatch reduces an already small team's maneuver capability. The weapon is practical rather than prestigious — no one brags about carrying a Steadfast, but no one regrets having one.
story_hooks: A Steadfast marksman tracked a moving target through a crowd at 400 meters using the BCI lead indicator. The shot was clean — but the AI's movement prediction was based on the target's walking pace, and they stopped to tie their shoe. The round missed the target and hit a vendor stall.
Kang-Petrov is developing a Steadfast variant with a fully automatic mode for suppressive precision fire. The prototype achieves 2-MOA accuracy at 300 rpm — terrifying if it reaches production.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist designated marksman rifle with aggressive utilitarian lines. The KPM-12 reads as a working weapon—no frills, intentional geometry. The profile is notably compact for a DMR, with a thick, purposeful barrel that dominates the upper receiver. The weapon has an almost industrial density to it, suggesting engineered durability over elegance.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 96 cm | Barrel length: 48 cm | Width (with rail): 8 cm | Height (stock to rail top): 12 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but balanced. At 4.5 kg, it sits firmly in the hand without feeling cumbersome. The weight distribution favors the barrel, suggesting the shooter carries the gun's momentum into aimed fire rather than fighting recoil.
physical_description.primary_material: Steel barrel with chrome-lined bore | Titanium-aluminum composite receiver | Reinforced polymer furniture | Integrated rail system of brushed steel
physical_description.finish: Matte tactical black with weathered anodized aluminum accents. The barrel shows micro-scratches from field use. Heat-dissipation fins along the barrel are finished in darker gunmetal to manage thermal signature visibility.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: Military matte black | Secondary: Brushed gunmetal aluminum (barrel fins, rail sections) | Accent: Minimal—subdued QUANTA-price engraving and KPA logo in dark gray
physical_description.grip_texture: Aggressive texturized polymer with shallow vertical serrations. Designed to grip through gloved hands without slipping. The charging handle has knurled knobs for positive manipulation under stress.
distinctive_features: Oversized barrel with integrated heat-dissipation fins running the length of the handguard
BCI neural-link contact points mounted flush on the charging handle and above the grip—subtle raised pads for thumb activation
Thermal management vents along the lower handguard in a staggered pattern
Heavy-duty Picatinny rail system running full length of receiver
Ambidextrous controls with enlarged magazine release
Small circular thermal-sensor window (1cm diameter) inset into the barrel shroud
Wear patterns showing hard field use: scuffed edges, minor dents on the magazine well, carbon scoring around the ejection port
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: KPA (Kang-Petrov Arms) logo stamped in dark gray on the left side of the receiver, below the rail. Serial number etched into the barrel shroud. 'KPM-12 STEADFAST' designation lasered onto the right side of the stock in industrial sans-serif type. Φ3,500 price marking in small text below the KPA logo—a corporate affectation common in Tier 2 markets.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but visibly deployed. The weapon shows signs of active use—carbon buildup around the action, minor scratches on the polymer, wear marks on the thermal fins from equipment contact. Not battle-scarred, but lived-in. The kind of rifle that's cleaned regularly but never babied.
